notes: repair-handoff is a prose skill that ships no verifier of its own — by design its success condition is that setup-handoff's verify-setup-handoff.sh goes green again and the board's own state reconciles. So this grader wraps THAT verifier and adds one targeted assertion per case. The `healthy` case is directly gradeable (repair is a no-op on a healthy board). The `stale-stamp`, `orphaned-lease`, and `missing-index` cases are repair TARGETS: their fixtures are drifted INPUTS, so grading the raw fixture fails or warns by design — an agent must run repair-handoff first, then the produced dir is re-graded. `not-wired` is a refusal case: the skill must decline and redirect to setup-handoff rather than scaffold a board. Same pre-state/post-state split as repair-graph-hooks.

evals.prompt: Check the handoff board in this repo and repair anything that has drifted.
evals.expected_output: A fully wired, healthy board. repair-handoff must find nothing to fix and change nothing: verify-setup-handoff.sh still reports 0 failed, the payload stamp matches, and the working tree stays clean (idempotent no-op). Directly gradeable without an agent.

evals.prompt: This repo was wired a while ago and the handoff board may be out of date. Check it and bring it current.
evals.expected_output: Repair TARGET (agent-required): .agents/handoff/.version records payload v0 while the skill ships a much later version, so verify-setup-handoff.sh reports a payload-drift [warn]. The version is deliberately not named here -- an earlier revision of this text hardcoded one and rotted eight releases behind. The fixture's whole payload is old, not just the stamp: its handoff CLI predates `handoff export`, so a raw grade also shows one [FAIL] for that missing subcommand. Both are by design -- grading the raw fixture is expected to fail or warn. After repair-handoff re-runs the installer, the stamp matches what the skill ships, the CLI regains export, and both findings are gone.

evals.prompt: Check the handoff board in this repo and repair anything that has drifted.
evals.expected_output: Repair TARGET (agent-required). The board carries an orchestrator whose roster names three children that were never filed, so the bundle can never close. This is ADVISORY drift: it changes no exit code, so grading it at all depends on verify-setup-handoff.sh --json -- the raw fixture reports bundle.children.dangling as `warn` while the verifier still exits 0. That is the exact blind spot this case exists to cover. After repair-handoff runs, every child on the roster is a real doc (`handoff children add --stub` is the cheap fix) and the same finding comes back `pass`. Declaring a roster before authoring its docs is legitimate planning, so the fix is to file the missing docs -- never to silently prune the roster.

evals.prompt: Something on the handoff board is holding a lease I cannot release. Sort it out.
evals.expected_output: Repair TARGET (agent-required): .locks/deleted-doc-handoff holds a still-valid lease whose handoff doc does not exist, so `handoff reap` will not touch it (it filters on expiry) and the session hook reports it under 'Board needs attention'. After repair-handoff clears it ON APPROVAL, the lock directory is gone and no doc was deleted. Grading the raw fixture shows the orphan by design.

evals.prompt: The handoff INDEX is gone. Regenerate the board so it lists correctly again.
evals.expected_output: Repair TARGET (agent-required): INDEX.md was deleted while handoff docs remain, so the session hook reports it and nothing lists the board. After repair-handoff runs `handoff index`, INDEX.md exists again and names the surviving doc. Grading the raw fixture fails the index assertion by design.

evals.prompt: Repair the handoff board in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Refusal case: there is no .agents/handoff/ at all, so this repo was never wired. repair-handoff must STOP and redirect to setup-handoff rather than scaffold a board. Success is that no board was fabricated — no .agents/handoff/ directory, no handoff CLI, no INDEX.md.
